title: fix(components): the date pickers and every Calendar read the display locale (objectui#10722)
body:
Fixes #10722
Clause-②: no

Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 5 (claim 5851804361, triage 5851675691). This run's session: `session_01KUxVUa7e39aNjhkKi1gsoy`.

## What was wrong

`useDisplayLocale.ts` says every date, number and currency renderer goes through it, and the `Intl` date faces have done so since objectui#10442 and objectui#10668. The date-fns and react-day-picker faces never did. They take a date-fns `Locale` OBJECT, not the BCP-47 tag the hook returns, and nothing turned one into the other. With none supplied, date-fns `format` and `DayPicker` answer in `enUS` under every display locale and every UI language.

Measured first (H1), on base `5c61e5241` with the pins below and the sources unmodified: an English UI with a `de-CH` display locale, date 2020-03-04. 6 of 10 pins failed; the 4 controls passed.

| face | base reading | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| form date picker label (`PPP`) | `March 4th, 2020` | `4. März 2020` |
| form date picker, authored `EEEE, d. MMMM yyyy` | `Wednesday, 4. March 2020` | `Mittwoch, 4. März 2020` |
| `DatePicker` component label | `March 4th, 2020` | `4. März 2020` |
| `Calendar` month caption | `March 2020` | `März 2020` |
| `Calendar` weekday heads | not asserted on base (the caption assertion fails first); base passes no locale, so they read as the en-US control, `Su Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa` | `Mo Di Mi Do Fr Sa So` |
| `ui:calendar` renderer caption | `March 2020` | `März 2020` |

For the card's date (2026-09-27) the label's call, date-fns `format(date, 'PPP')`, gives `September 27th, 2026`; with `de` it gives `27. September 2026`.

## The choice: (a), on the four axes

The triage (5851675691) left (a) or (b) to the claiming seat, under two constraints: `DatePickerSchema.format` keeps its meaning, a date-fns pattern, and is still honoured; and no date-fns locale is bundled eagerly. Measured against them:

- **(b) cannot hold constraint 1 and fix the face at once.** `PPP` needs a date-fns `Locale` to be spelled in German. Read through `Intl.DateTimeFormat(tag, { dateStyle: 'long' })` instead, `de-CH` gives `4. März 2020`, but `en-US` gives `March 4, 2020`, not today's `March 4th, 2020`. So the en-US control changes, and `PPP` stops meaning what date-fns documents. An authored pattern with textual tokens (`EEEE, d. MMMM yyyy`) stays English under (b), because date-fns still formats it with no locale. The `date-picker` registration's `defaultProps` write `format: 'PPP'`, so a designer-made picker is on exactly that path. The week start would also stay Sunday under (b), unless it read `Intl.Locale` week info.
- **(a) holds both.** The pattern is still date-fns's and is honoured as written, now spelled in the display locale. No locale is in any eager chunk (see Bundle).

The four axes:

- **Actual business need.** The display locale is a free BCP-47 tag: the tenant's or user's localization locale (the spec's `LocaleSchema` is a free string), or else one of the ten UI languages. Every picker user under a German UI reads English today. (a) answers every tag date-fns has a locale for. (b) answers every tag `Intl` knows, but only for the default label, and not for an authored pattern.
- **Long-term soundness.** Under (a) one date-fns `Locale` drives every date-fns-backed reading: the label pattern, the caption, the weekday names, the week start, and `DayPicker`'s day-button aria text (`PPPP`). It comes from one resolver. (b) splits one face across two formatting engines, which is how an authored pattern and the caption would come to disagree.
- **Keeping AI from writing wrong metadata.** `format` keeps one meaning, a date-fns pattern an author can look up in date-fns's docs. (b) would make `PPP` mean something date-fns does not document. No metadata key moves.
- **Startup focus.** No new prop, no export, no schema change, no dependency change: one private module and a two-line declared patch. The locale table is date-fns's own list, not a product choice of which languages to support.

The named cost of (a): the first paint of a session whose locale has not loaded yet reads `enUS`, and re-renders once the locale arrives. The "falls back to enUS" pin measures it: first render `March 4th, 2020`, then `4 mars 2020` for `fr-CH`. It happens once per locale per page lifetime. Later mounts read the loaded locale on their first render.

## What changed

- `packages/components/src/lib/date-fns-locale.ts` (new, not exported). It turns the tag into a date-fns locale code. The chain is the tag as given, then `language-region` and `language-script` from `Intl.Locale#maximize`, then the bare language, then `en-US`. So `de-CH` reads `de`, `en` reads `en-US`, `zh` reads `zh-CN`, and `zh-Hant` reads `zh-TW`. There is one lazy loader per date-fns locale: 94 literal `import("date-fns/locale/…")` calls. `enUS` is the one static import. `useDisplayDateLocale()` returns the resolved locale, and `enUS` while it loads. A failed load is not memoised.
- `packages/components/src/ui/calendar.tsx`: `DayPicker` gets `locale={displayDateLocale}` before `{...props}`, so a caller's `locale` still wins. This is a No-Touch file (AGENTS.md commandment 7), so the edit is a declared patch in `scripts/shadcn-local-patches.mjs`, family `calendar`, two patches. Both anchors were written from registry bytes vendored as `scripts/__tests__/fixtures/shadcn-registry/calendar.registry.txt`. Those bytes were captured at shadcn-ui/ui `8a7701ec2`, the four other fixtures' commit, from raw.githubusercontent.com, since the registry host answers 403 here. The same capture reproduces `slider`'s recorded sha256 byte for byte. The patch engine wrote the shipped file.
- `custom/date-picker.tsx` and `renderers/form/date-picker.tsx` pass the locale to `format`.
- `shadcn-components.json`: calendar's `localEdits` now names the declared patch.
- `.changeset/10722-date-fns-display-locale.md`: `'@object-ui/components': patch`.

## Census (H2)

Method: `git grep` over `packages/*/src` and `apps/*/src`, tests excluded, for `date-fns` and `react-day-picker` imports and for Calendar JSX mounts. It found 2 date-fns `format` call sites, 1 `DayPicker` mount (`ui/calendar.tsx`) and 5 `Calendar` mounts.

| # | site | what it formats | locale before | locale after |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `custom/date-picker.tsx`, `DatePicker` | trigger label, `PPP` | enUS | display locale |
| 2 | same, its popover `Calendar` | caption, weekday heads, week start | enUS | display locale |
| 3 | `renderers/form/date-picker.tsx` (`date-picker`) | trigger label, `schema.format`, default `PPP` | enUS | display locale; the pattern is honoured |
| 4 | same, its popover `Calendar` | caption, weekday heads, week start | enUS | display locale |
| 5 | `renderers/form/calendar.tsx` (`ui:calendar`) | caption, weekday heads | a `locale` in its props, else enUS | a `locale` in its props, else display locale |
| 6 | plugin-calendar `CalendarView` header popover | caption, weekday heads | enUS | display locale (see Acceptance notes) |
| 7 | plugin-dashboard `DashboardFilterBar` custom range (2 months) | caption, weekday heads | enUS | display locale |
| 8 | `ui/calendar.tsx` `formatMonthDropdown` | month dropdown names | machine locale (`"default"`) | unchanged: declared in `machineLocaleCensus-9909`, and reached only under a dropdown `captionLayout` that no first-party caller sets |

Rows 6 and 7 are reached through `Calendar` itself, so neither plugin file is edited. Neither passes its own locale or format to `Calendar`.

## Week start (H4)

It moves. A calendar under a display locale whose date-fns locale starts the week on Monday (`de`, `fr`, `en-GB`, …) now starts on Monday. That is the display locale's own reading, not a new rule: `DayPicker`'s week start follows its locale. `en-US` still starts on Sunday. Pinned: `Mo Di Mi Do Fr Sa So` against `Su Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa`.

## A caller's locale (H5)

Kept, because the default sits before the `{...props}` spread. Pinned: `locale: it` under a `de-CH` display locale reads `marzo 2020`.

## Bundle

The package was built with `pnpm turbo run build --filter @object-ui/components` twice. "Before" is the reverse-verification tree: the three consuming files at base, and the new module unreferenced, so it is not bundled. "After" is final head `fc7bcdd5d`, byte-identical to the pre-merge after-build. Sizes are the file's bytes and its `gzip -9` bytes.

| file | before raw / gzip | after raw / gzip |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `dist/index.js` | 560,972 / 133,463 | 568,187 / 135,025 |
| `dist/index.umd.cjs` | 455,300 / 120,574 | 461,383 / 122,074 |

Both builds keep `date-fns` external. After the change, each file has 94 external `import()` calls of `date-fns/locale/…` and one static `date-fns/locale/en-US`. Neither file carries any locale body: `März` and `Mittwoch` have 0 hits in each. `dist/index.d.ts` is byte-identical before and after. The dist gains `lib/date-fns-locale.d.ts`, which neither `index.d.ts` nor the `exports` map reaches.

Chunk graph: I ran a minimal consumer build (vite 8 / rolldown) of `ui/calendar.tsx` and `custom/date-picker.tsx` from source, once with default chunking and once with the console's `vendor-react` and `ui-components` groups. Both give 94 lazy chunks, one locale each, and none of them in the eager closure. The only locale module in the eager closure is `en-US`, which date-fns `format` and `DayPicker` already import as their default. The lazy `de` chunk is about 4 KB unminified.

NOT MEASURED: the console's own build and its eager-closure budget (`check:eager-closure`, the `ui-components` ceiling). Those are CI's Build & E2E. The eager addition is the loader table and the resolver. The package dist grew by +1,562 gzip bytes, which gives the order of it.

## Tests

- New pins in `packages/components/src/__tests__/date-picker-display-locale-10722.test.tsx`, 10 rows. On base: exit 1, 6 failed and 4 passed (the four are the controls: the en-US label, the unknown and malformed tag, the en-US calendar, and the caller's locale). After: exit 0, 10 passed.
- `packages/components/src/__tests__/date-fns-locale-10722.test.ts` holds each of the 95 keys to a loaded locale whose `code` is that key, and holds the chain rows and the ten UI languages.
- The calendar family is covered by `scripts/__tests__/shadcn-local-patches.test.ts`: the new fixture entry, the family ids, the anchors against the registry bytes, and the shipped file carrying both markers.
- Reverse verification on committed `163fc72e5`, with a trap-restored script and absolute paths. The three consuming files were checked out at base, and `useDisplayDateLocale` then counted 0 in each on disk. The pins went red: 1 file failed, 6 failed and 4 passed, with the same six messages as base. After the restore, `git hash-object` equals the HEAD blob for all three files and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- Final union on head `fc7bcdd5d` (after merging `origin/main` `c3a26ccda`), through `os-verify-lock`, exit 0:
  - `pnpm turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/components`: 9 of 9 tasks.
  - `pnpm type-check:scripts`: passed.
  - `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over `packages/components/`, `packages/plugin-calendar/` and `packages/plugin-dashboard/`, plus the 7 outside files that name a changed file: 504 files passed and 1 skipped; 4950 tests passed and 17 skipped.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists both new test files and the new module.
- ESLint, plain form, on the 8 changed ts/tsx/mjs files: exit 0, 0 errors, 1 warning. The warning is the pre-existing `any` in the `date-picker` registration signature, not on an added line. Narrowing proof: `isPathIgnored` is false for all 8 files; `--format json` counts 8 files; `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`; and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem.
- Gates, each exit 0 on `fc7bcdd5d`: `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check-changeset-presence` and `changeset:check`.
  - `check:changeset-claims` names two pending changesets that mention `shadcn-components.json` (7397 and 9569). Both paragraphs still hold: the `chart` entry is unchanged, and nothing about stylesheet sources moved.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:readme-exports`. Its population collapsed because 28 packages are unbuilt in this worktree (a prerequisite, not a verdict). This diff touches no README and no export.

## Acceptance notes

- `CalendarView`'s authored `locale` prop reaches its grid, but not its header popover. The popover mounts `Calendar` with no `locale`, so it read enUS before and reads the display locale now, even when a host sets a different `locale`. Forwarding the authored locale would need a tag-to-`Locale` resolution in plugin-calendar: either an export from components (ruled out on this card) or a date-fns dependency there. Noted, not filed.
- `formatMonthDropdown` in `ui/calendar.tsx` still uses the machine locale (census row 8). A dropdown caller would override it through `formatters`.
- `DayPicker`'s own aria words (`Go to the Next Month`, `Today, …`) come from react-day-picker's English `labels`. They are UI-language strings, not a display-locale face. react-day-picker ships translated `labels` under `react-day-picker/locale`, which imports from the `date-fns/locale` barrel. Observation only.

## Deviations

- **Surface.** The claim names `ui/calendar.tsx`. AGENTS.md commandment 7 makes that a No-Touch file whose sanctioned edit is a declared patch, and that brought four files outside the named surface: `scripts/shadcn-local-patches.mjs`, `scripts/__tests__/shadcn-local-patches.test.ts`, the vendored `scripts/__tests__/fixtures/shadcn-registry/calendar.registry.txt`, and `packages/components/shadcn-components.json`. None is governed (`check-governed-queue-guard --test`: NOT GOVERNED, 11 paths), and no open PR touches any of them (14 open PRs re-read before this PR was opened).
- **"Before" build.** The before build was measured on the reverse-verification tree, not on a separate base checkout. The new module is present there, but no file imports it, so it is not bundled (0 locale imports in that dist).
- **Base weekday heads.** Not asserted on base (see the H1 table).
